items.place: approx. 53°N 9°E, lower Weser–Elbe area, Lower Saxony, Germany
items.note: As printed, this falls on land near Bremen. The positions are rounded to whole degrees, so it is probably a ship in the Elbe/Weser approaches, or the longitude is misprinted. The land birds (Crested Lark, Yellowhammer) suggest a coast close by. It shares its example text with n=1458 and may be one entry 'between' the two positions.

items.place: approx. 54°N 10°E, Schleswig-Holstein (Kiel / Eckernförde Bay), Germany
items.note: As printed, this is on or just off the Kiel Bay coast. Same caveats as n=1457. Check whether the two positions belong to one entry.

items.place: At sea, position garbled (probably tropical South Atlantic)
items.note: The OCR 'se? 43°.8. | 92350" W.' can't be recovered. It could be something like 3°43′S 9°23′50″W, which would fit the Sooty Tern sightings at 1°S 13°W and 9°23′S 3°22′W. Read the page scan.

notes: None of the 22 Ocean Notes names (1884) is a station of the scheme. 19 are places: 16 ship positions, plus Bijagós, Tarifa and the Terschelling light-vessel. Cape Point, Cape St Vincent and Spitsbergen are also on their own lines but are not counted in those 19, which covers 22. The 2 ship-name items (Marathon) are none. Things to check: (1) n=1473: the position is garbled OCR; read the scan. (2) n=1457/1458 (53°N 9°E, 54°N 10°E): both fall on land in north Germany as printed and share their example text. Check whether they are one entry 'between' two positions, a ship going up the Elbe, or a misprinted longitude. (3) n=120 'Bejouga Islands' is read as the Bijagós/Bissagos (old 'Bijugas'); confirm. (4) n=1073 'Schelling light-vessel' is the Dutch Terschelling light-vessel, not a station of the scheme; check that it was a passing ship's sighting. (5) n=1221/1222 'Steamship Marathon' (33 observations) are typed none. If you want them placed, give each a position from its date or a nearby lat/long. The 1884 route (Biscay → Cape St Vincent → Madeira → West Africa → equator → South Atlantic → Cape Point → Algoa Bay) fits a voyage to the Cape. (6) The minus sign before 9° in n=13 is assumed to be OCR noise.
